reference.title: Vertical text, ruby, emphasis and shadows
reference.shortdesc: This reference lists the properties and the display values that CSSMedia uses to write text in vertical lines, to annotate it with ruby, and to mark and shade it.

row.entry: The direction in which lines run and in which they follow each other. In vertical-rl the lines are vertical and go from the right to the left. In vertical-lr they go from the left to the right. In sideways-rl and sideways-lr all the text is turned: lines go from the right and from the left, and the text reads downward and upward. On the root element, it sets the writing mode of the page. It is inherited.
horizontal-tb, vertical-rl, vertical-lr, sideways-rl or sideways-lr

How the characters of a vertical line are turned. mixed sets the characters of scripts that are written vertically, such as Chinese and Japanese, upright and turns the others a quarter clockwise. upright sets all of them upright, one under another. sideways turns all of them. It is inherited.
mixed, upright or sideways
An older property that makes the same choice as text-orientation, and that CSSMedia reads as that property. auto is mixed, 0deg and 0 are upright, and 90deg and 90 are sideways.
auto, 0deg, 0, 90deg or 90

Sets several characters side by side in the space of one, upright, inside a vertical line. all combines the text of the element. digits combines each run of digits that has as many digits as the integer or fewer. The result fits in a square of one em, with half-width forms for two characters when the font has them. It works in every vertical writing mode, the sideways modes included, and has no effect in horizontal-tb. It is inherited.
none, all or digits with an optional integer from 2 to 4, which is 2 when it is left out
The direction of the text along the line. In a vertical line, ltr goes down and rtl goes up. In sideways-lr it is the other way around. It is inherited.
ltr or rtl
How an element takes part in the ordering of text that mixes directions.
normal, embed, isolate, bidi-override, isolate-override or plaintext

How strict the rules are that keep some characters off the start or the end of a line: closing brackets and stops do not start a line, opening brackets do not end one, and a dash or an ellipsis of two characters is not split. They apply in vertical lines as they do in horizontal ones. normal and strict also keep small kana, the long vowel mark and iteration marks off the start of a line and do not split an ellipsis; loose allows those breaks. In Chinese and Japanese, normal and loose let 〜 and ゠ start a line. anywhere allows a break after every character.
auto, loose, normal, strict or anywhere

When the blank half of full-width brackets, commas, stops and middle dots is removed. normal keeps an opening bracket full at the start of a line, makes a closing mark half at the end of a line only when the line does not fit otherwise, and removes one blank between two marks that stand together. space-all keeps all marks full. trim-start makes opening brackets half at the start of every line, and space-first does so except on the first line and after a line feed. trim-both also makes closing marks half at the end of every line. trim-all makes all of them half everywhere. It is inherited.
space-all, normal, space-first, trim-start, trim-both or trim-all

Where an underline is drawn. auto puts it just under the alphabetic baseline, from-font where the font says, and under under the whole text; in a vertical line all three are on the left. In a vertical line, left puts it outside the text on the left and right outside the text on the right, and then the overline moves to the left. In horizontal text and in the sideways modes, left and right act as auto. It is inherited.
auto, or from-font or under with left or right
How far the underline is moved away from the place that text-underline-position gives it. A percentage is of the font size. It is inherited.
auto, a length or a percentage
Value of display
The element is
A ruby: a group of bases with their annotations. It sits on a line of text.
The text that is annotated.
One annotation.
A group of bases that stands on one level.
A group of annotations that stands on one level, over or under the bases.

Where the annotations are. over is above the bases in horizontal text and on the right in vertical text. under is the other side. alternate puts the first level over, or under with alternate under, and the next levels on the other side of the level before. inter-character puts each annotation after its base in horizontal text, and acts as over in vertical text. It is inherited.
alternate or over or under, with alternate optional beside them, or inter-character

How the content of a base or an annotation is spread when it is narrower than its column. start puts it at the start. center centers it. space-between spreads the characters over the whole column. space-around does the same with half a space at each end. It is inherited.
start, center, space-between or space-around

Whether the annotations of a level are shown as one annotation over all the bases. merge does it always. auto does it when an annotation is wider than its base. separate keeps them apart. It is inherited.
separate, merge or auto
Lets an annotation that is wider than its base reach over the kana beside it. The reach is at most half the size of the annotation. none keeps it inside the column. It is inherited.
auto or none

The mark that is put beside each character. filled or open alone gives a circle in horizontal text and in the sideways modes, and a sesame in vertical-rl and vertical-lr. A shape alone is filled. A string gives a mark that is the first character of the string. It is inherited.
none, filled or open with dot, circle, double-circle, triangle or sesame, or a string
The color of the marks. It is inherited.
A color
Sets text-emphasis-style and text-emphasis-color together.
A style and a color, in any order
See the two properties

The side where the marks are. In horizontal text and in the sideways modes, over and under choose the side of the line. In vertical-rl and vertical-lr, right and left choose it. The marks stand outside a ruby on the same side, even one that is hidden or empty, and outside an underline or an overline. It is inherited.
over or under, and right or left
The characters that get no mark: spaces, punctuation, symbols and the characters that are set narrow. It is inherited.
One or more of spaces, punctuation, symbols and narrow

One or more shadows of the text and of its decorations. Each one has a horizontal and a vertical offset, a spread and a color. In a font that you embed with @font-face, it can also have a blur and be inset. The offsets are on the page whatever the writing mode: a positive horizontal offset is to the right. The first shadow is on top. It is inherited.
none or a comma separated list of shadows
